name: Pisolithus arhizus

ecology.substrate: hot, dry, acid or metal-rich soil around tree roots (unchecked)

size_cm.note: fruit body width; it stands 5 to 16 cm high

notes: One file for a species group (syn. P. tinctorius), cosmopolitan only as a group; long-distance type is reported for the family (unchecked). Reported (unchecked) to be the most used commercial inoculant, to have a sequenced genome and yellow rhizomorphs, and to tolerate mine waste.

tip_speed.note: worked out, not reported as a rate: two 5 mm plugs of P. tinctorius set 3 cm apart on MMN agar at 25 C met after about 12 days (Baptista et al. 2021, In vitro interactions between the ectomycorrhizal Pisolithus tinctorius and the saprotroph Hypholoma fasciculare fungi, Mycology 12(3):216-229, https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/21501203.2021.1876778). Each colony edge covered (30 - 5) / 2 = 12.5 mm in 12 days, about 1.0 mm/day or 43 um/h. Assumes the 3 cm is centre to centre. At 25 C, below the 28 C optimum; not corrected

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Marx D.H., Bryan W.C., Davey C.B. 1970, Influence of temperature on aseptic synthesis of ectomycorrhizae by Thelephora terrestris and Pisolithus tinctorius on loblolly pine, Forest Science 16(4):424-431
t_opt.note: mycelial growth in pure culture was greatest at 28 C (abstract). Optima of single isolates ranged from 21 to 32 C in Cline, France & Reid 1987, Can. J. Bot. 65:869-875 (https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/10.1139/b87-119)

t_max.note: no upper limit is stated in the abstracts read. Ectomycorrhizae formed best at 34 C, the hottest treatment (Marx et al. 1970, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1093/forestscience/16.4.424), and this species grew best of four at the hotter treatments of a 16 to 38 C series (Cline et al. 1987, https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/10.1139/b87-119), so the limit is above 34 C; 38 C, the hottest temperature tested there, is used and may be too low
